look_here_first: Flip the flower head over. The quickest field mark is the involucre: the four broad outer phyllaries form a conspicuous square/collar-like base around the head. Then confirm the yellow ray florets, large disc florets with paleae, and the leafy upright habit.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: upright perennial herb with leafy stems

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves mostly cauline, opposite in much of the genus; local plants can have irregularly toothed to pinnatifid blades

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: outer four involucral bracts/phyllaries broad and conspicuous, producing the characteristic squarebud/collar appearance

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: inner phyllaries smaller and more scarious

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: receptacle paleate, with a sharp bract/palea subtending individual disc florets

key_traits.label: Family training
key_traits.text: High-value Asteraceae teaching species: identify the family from the capitulum/ray+disc architecture, then use the underside of the head—the square outer phyllaries/involucre—as the genus/species-level field shortcut.

key_traits.label: Video training
key_traits.text: Joey explicitly flips the head over and uses the four broad square-ish phyllaries as the diagnostic cue among several similar yellow composites.
